definition: Elements that keep the same place across screens or pages.
include: Persistent panels, fixed navigation, repeated page structure.
exclude: Visual similarity with no navigation role.

definition: Distinct routes into a feature or a piece of content.
include: Banners, cards, buttons and headings that start a path.

definition: Labels, headings and markers that help someone place themselves.
include: Category headings, tabs, step numbers, legends, page labels.
exclude: Content text read for its own sake.

definition: Ways back to familiar ground after a detour.
include: Back arrows, close buttons, 'start chat' after browsing, home tab.
exclude: Exit used as a retention device (code AG.exit).

definition: The single element that dominates a screen or page.
include: Hero portrait, large title, central count.

definition: Colour used to mark the next action or the important item.
include: Gradient buttons, red prices, a highlighted chip.
exclude: Colour used only for identity (code SY.colour).

definition: Size differences that rank information.
include: Large selected value beside small neighbours, giant type.

definition: Movement or staged disclosure that pulls attention.
include: Spin results, reveal animation, breathing pulse.

definition: How numbers, prices, durations and counts are set.
include: Price columns, timers, statistics, dates.

definition: Different typefaces or weights doing different jobs.
include: Display vs text faces, italics for a second language.

definition: Two or more languages on the same surface.
include: Polish/Vietnamese pairs, Polish/English menus, EN/PL posters.

definition: Icons, signs and emoji that replace or support words.
include: Dietary signs, emoji cards, QR codes, icon rows.

definition: How much text competes on one surface.
include: Dense lists, long descriptions, crowded columns.

definition: Steps people can skip without penalty.
include: Skip links, optional notes, optional ads.

definition: Information that explains price, probability or terms before a decision.
include: Drop rates, pity counters, plan prices, 'prices include VAT'.

definition: Controls that interrupt an activity and explain the consequence.
include: Pause/quit buttons, close icons, leave dialogs.

definition: Prompts that lower the effort of a first action.
include: Suggested replies, presets, default durations, guided sessions.

definition: Acknowledgement after finishing something.
include: Result screens, congratulation, mood check-in.
exclude: Generic success toasts with no content.

definition: Records of past activity.
include: Calendars, session lists, streak badges, totals.

definition: Screens that explain loading, offline or empty conditions.
include: Splash loader, offline screen, error recovery.

definition: Visible distance to a target.
include: Pity counter, 'day 1 of 5', scrubber, stamps on a loyalty card.

definition: A limited palette applied with rules.
include: Brand gradient, red-and-cream, three pastel accents, cobalt.

definition: A graphic element repeated across pieces.
include: Dotted dragon, ξ mark, yellow contour, starburst.

definition: Consistent type styles across a set.
include: Rounded headings plus italics, heavy grotesque titles.

definition: Elements that tie a series while each piece varies.
include: Poster templates, shared footer, triptych treatment.

definition: The identity extended to objects and formats beyond the main piece.
include: Bag, box, loyalty card, apron, tees.
exclude: The core menu or screen itself.

definition: References to national or cultural heritage.
include: Traditional Ukrainian dress, Vietnamese dish names, Diia.

definition: Insider symbols a group recognises.
include: ξ, binary, keyboard keys, faculty room numbers.
exclude: Signs aimed at the general public.

definition: Adapting content for a language or market.
include: EN versions of PL posters, EN switcher, VAT note.

definition: Work that expresses a feeling or a position.
include: War response, manifesto, handwritten words.

definition: Meeting or collecting new content by chance or choice.
include: Gacha banners, character library, rate-up.

definition: Gems, points, passes and free rewards.
include: Gem balance, tasks, packs, loyalty stamps.
exclude: Prices for real goods without a reward loop (code AG.odds).

definition: Where purchase prompts appear and how loudly.
include: Shop modal, first-purchase bonus, trial plan.
exclude: Purchase information in terms and footers.

definition: Rewards or reasons to start.
include: 50 gems on sign-up, free trial, free ticket code.

definition: Muted colour, space and slow pacing.
include: Pastel blocks, soft circles, quiet lists.

definition: Energy, surprise and humour.
include: Stars, bursts, spirals, rotated type.

definition: Pressure, conflict or time limits.
include: Countdown timers, handwritten scrawl, sickle.

definition: Supportive, non-judging wording or feedback.
include: 'Calm in 5 days', 'Only you see this', positive results.

definition: Products or traditions named as inspiration.
include: Telegram, Romance Club, Diia, gacha games.

definition: Given limits and the job to be done.
include: Only the KSI mark was given; corridor viewing; old menu.

definition: What the designer wanted a decision to achieve.
include: 'I wanted…', 'The aim was…'.

definition: Comparison with a previous version.
include: Old menu pages, redesign comparisons.

definition: What the designer was responsible for.
include: Role statements, deliverables, printed vs concept.
exclude: Team or client work not done by the designer.

definition: Two strong elements that may fight for the first look.
include: Portrait vs cost, motif vs dates, dragon vs list.

definition: Mechanics that may push repeated paying.
include: Random rewards, timers on banners, bonus packs.

definition: Signs that may be read differently by different people.
include: Insider symbols, handwriting, emoji, abstract icons.

definition: Choices that may exclude some readers.
include: Low-contrast small text, colour-only meaning, tiny print.

definition: A concrete task for a future interview or test.
include: 'Find…', 'Compare…', 'Set the timer…'.

definition: What the materials cannot show on their own.
include: Statements about outcomes that need data.
